newsitem.title: USA: USDA pegs Brazil orange juice output at 1.25 Mln T.
newsitem.headline: USDA pegs Brazil orange juice output at 1.25 Mln T.

text.p: Brazil will produce a record 1.25 million tonnes of orange juice in 1997/98, the U.S. Agriculture Department forecast Friday, up slightly from an earlier estimate of 1.22 million tonnes.
In its World Horticultural Trade circular, USDA repeated its estimate that Brazil would export 1.16 million tonnes of orange juice in 1997/98.

"Total Brazilian orange juice production for 1997 is forecast at 1.25 million tonnes, a 10 percent increase over the previous year," USDA said. "Brazilian exports in the 1997 season are forecast to increase two percent to 1.16 million tonnes...mainly due to expected export growth in Eastern Europe and Asian markets."

The previous USDA estimate was made June 2. An unofficial report written by the U.S. agricultural attache in Sao Paulo and released June 30 pegged orange juice output at 1.25 million tonnes for Brazil in 1997/98.
In its new estimate, USDA said Brazil would see record crops and processing in 1997/98.
Brazil is the major competitor to Florida in orange juice production and U.S. market supplier.
